evidence:
packaging/freeze-native-image.sh:41-42
  lz4=$build/lib/libfn-lz4.so
  [ -s "$lz4" ] || { echo "freeze-native-image: missing $lz4 (tools/build_lz4.sh)" >&2; exit 4; }
and :80 cp -L "$lz4" "$out/lib/libfn-lz4.so"; packaging/install-native.sh:52,59,86-93,181 require and copy it the same way; tools/extract/core.sh:80 exports FN_LZ4_LIBRARY=$LIB/libfn-lz4.so. tools/build_lz4.sh was deleted in 7cf1972e2 ('LZ4 retirement'), no host/native/lz4.lisp exists, and tools/build_native_host.sh:104-129 builds only mldsa65, deflate and blake3 into build/lib.
fix: Remove the lz4 requirement and copy from freeze-native-image.sh, install-native.sh (both branches and the inventory line) and tools/extract/core.sh/build.sh, with the same change that retired LZ4. If LZ4 is coming back, restore its build script and have build_native_host.sh build it. Fix the stale '(tools/build_lz4.sh)' reference in build_deflate.sh:10 too.
notes: 2026-10-03 Codex source reconciliation: e6b827d210ec8d539250ccf668a8afddb7b756fb is an ancestor of dev 9af0cd1a9. This is a source-landing receipt only; native/proof completion is not inferred, and existing residuals and evidence requirements remain.
reviewer: packaging/freeze-native-image.sh:41-42 requires build/lib/libfn-lz4.so and copies it at :80. tools/build_lz4.sh and host/native/lz4.lisp are both gone (git log: 7cf1972e2 LZ4 retirement). tools/build_native_host.sh:104-129 builds only mldsa65, deflate and blake3. release-tarball.sh:203-212 builds from a fresh git archive, and served/lib is a symlink to TREE/build/lib (tools/extract/core.sh:97), so freeze exits 4 on a clean tree. tools/extract/build.sh:66-69 also hard-requires libfn-lz4.so, and install-native.sh:87-93 does the same. A long-lived tree with a stale .so would bundle that untracked binary instead. The failure is loud and it blocks releases.
scenario: release-tarball.sh (first form) unpacks a fresh git archive, so build/lib holds only the three libraries build_native_host.sh makes. Step 3's freeze (release-tarball.sh:211) exits 4 with 'missing ... libfn-lz4.so (tools/build_lz4.sh)', naming a script that no longer exists, so no Linux or OpenBSD release can be cut from a clean tree. In a long-lived tree where an old build/lib/libfn-lz4.so survives, the freeze succeeds instead. It then bundles that stale, untracked binary into libexec/fn/lib and hashes it into SHA256SUMS and native-artifacts.txt as part of the release, although it was not built from REV's source.
title: The release pipeline requires libfn-lz4.so, but LZ4 was retired and nothing builds it, so a clean release fails or ships an orphan binary
